cards.front: Which part of an HTTP response tells you whether the request worked?
cards.back: The status code, for example `200` means OK and `404` means Not Found.

cards.front: Which Linux file shows the DNS server your machine asks?
Which HTTP method sends data in the body to create something new on the server?
cards.back: `POST`, for example submitting a sign-up form.

cards.front: What does an IP address identify?
cards.back: A computer on a network, like the street address of a building.

cards.front: Look up the IP address for the name `example.com` from the terminal
Which HTTP header says what format the body is in?
Which HTTP method fetches data without changing anything on the server?
cards.back: `GET`, for example loading a web page or reading a record from an API.

cards.front: Two programs run on the same computer and share its IP address. What tells their traffic apart?
cards.back: The port number: each program listens on its own port, like apartment numbers in one building.

cards.front: Which `curl` flag also prints the response status line and headers, not just the body?
Which Linux file lets you map a name to an IP address by hand?
Which port does PostgreSQL listen on by default?
In networking, what is a client?
cards.back: The program that starts the conversation by sending a request, like your web browser or `curl`.

cards.front: After DNS returns the IP address, does your traffic go through the DNS server?
cards.back: No, DNS only returns the address; your computer then connects to that address directly.Your computerDNS serverexample.com?Web serverconnects directlyIP address

cards.front: In HTTP, who speaks first, and what comes back?
cards.back: The client sends a request first; the server answers it with one response.clientserver1. request2. response

cards.front: What does the first digit of an HTTP status code tell you?
cards.back: The kind of outcome: 2 success, 3 redirect, 4 the client's mistake, 5 the server's fault.CodeMeaningExample2xxsuccess200 OK3xxredirect301 Moved Permanently4xxclient error404 Not Found5xxserver error500 Internal Server Error

cards.front: Which IP address always points back to your own machine?
In `192.168.1.10:8080`, which part is the port?
cards.back: `8080`, the number after the colon; `192.168.1.10` is the IP address.

cards.front: What does DNS do?
cards.back: It turns a name like `example.com` into the IP address your computer needs to connect.

cards.front: Can one program be both a client and a server?
cards.back: Yes: a web app is a server to browsers and a client when it queries its database.browserweb apprequestdatabaserequest

cards.front: Is a server a special kind of machine?
cards.back: No, a server is a role: any program that waits for requests and answers them. Your laptop can run one.
